title: Terraform module: GPU orchestration + safe upgrades for dual autoscaler (ASG + Karpenter)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module that manages GPU node groups in private VPCs and supports a dual-autoscaler operating mode (ASG + Karpenter) with robust upgrade and health-check primitives. The module must support: 1) safe driver/kernel upgrades for GPU instances with pre-drain/post-drain hooks; 2) canary capacity and staged rollouts; 3) health-check policies that gate node termination and replacement; 4) transparent observability hooks for Console dashboards and alerting; 5) a migration path from existing nodegroup modules with minimal customer downtime. Rationale: customers running Private deployments require predictable GPU availability and safe upgrades. Existing modules handle provisioning but lack coordinated upgrade semantics and dual-autoscaler orchestration for Private (VPC) environments. This module unifies those concerns into a single terraform module and ops runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes variables for dual_autoscaler_mode (off | asg_primary | karpenter_primary | hybrid)
Module supports pre_drains and post_drains scripts/containers with configurable timeouts
Upgrade path: cluster can apply a driver upgrade plan with <=5% p99 request failure increase in canary zone
Health-check policy prevents node termination when gpu-memory-pressure or driver-failure metrics exceed thresholds
Integration tests (infra) validate canary rolling upgrade in a private VPC with simulated load
Module outputs stable identifiers for Console (nodepool_id, autoscaler_policy_id, upgrade_run_id)
terraform_interface_summary: Variables: name_prefix, vpc_id, subnet_ids, instance_type, gpu_type, node_count_min, node_count_max, dual_autoscaler_mode, canary_percent, pre_drain_hook_docker_image, post_drain_hook_docker_image, node_health_thresholds (map encoded as JSON string), kms_key_arn, tags. Outputs: nodepool_id, autoscaler_policy_id, node_group_arn, upgrade_plan_manifest (base64). The module will call a small bootstrap userdata that registers a health-check agent with the control-plane (signed token).
migration_plan: 1) Add module to staging account and create a shadow nodepool with dual_autoscaler_mode=hybrid and canary_percent=10. 2) Run synthetic load against canary, validate metrics and IO. 3) Switch traffic incrementally (canary -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%). 4) If metric regressions detected, abort using automatic rollback policy and reassign ASG capacity. 5) After successful run, decommission legacy nodegroup via terraform state move and plan. Note: migration scripts are provided in scripts/migrate-legacy-nodegroup.sh in the repo.
testing_plan: Unit: terraform fmt & validate on CI. Integration: ephemeral infra deploy in CI account with small GPU instance (g4dn.xlarge equivalent), run driver-install and pre/post drain hooks. Chaos tests: inject node failure, simulate driver OOM, and assert rollbacks. Performance: run throughput test to ensure canary < 5% regression. Observability: verify Console dashboards populated and alerts fire on simulated health failures.
runbook: Runbook highlights: - Start upgrade: create upgrade_run via Terraform variable upgrade_run=true and set canary_percent. - Monitor Console 'GPU Nodepools' dashboard: node readiness, gpu_driver_version, kernel_errors. - If canary fails, set upgrade_abort=true in module inputs to trigger automatic rollback. - For emergency rollback, use apply with legacy_nodegroup=true to reattach traffic. - Post-upgrade: verify node kubelet logs, GPU driver metrics, and evicted pod counts. - Contact oncall: infra-sre@redwood.ai
